paragraphs.text: Prompt polishing for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI (dsh 0.2.x desktop runtime): concise rewrites, a b
uilt-in configuration page, and a route-leak fix. A derivative of dsh-prompt-enhance.
# dsh-prompt-polish
**Prompt polishing for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI** — one click (or one shortcut) turns a rough co
mposer draft into a directly usable prompt, and your original draft is always preserved.

> ### Derivative work — read this first
>
> `dsh-prompt-polish` is a **modified, unofficial derivati
ve of `dsh-prompt-enhance`** by its author (Apache-2.0). Upstream version **0.2.7** is the base of t

his project's `1.0.0`.
>
> **What this fork adds:** the plugin is actually *configurable* on the dsh
`0.2.x` runtime (upstream's configuration wiring had been removed from the harness, so its settings
were silently unreachable), it ships its own configuration page, it no longer leaks its HTTP route
when the entry is remounted, it drops pre-0.2 support, and the built-in rewrite strategy is the conc

ise one. The full list is in Differences from upstream and CHANGELOG.md.
>
> **Not endorsed.** This
is not an official release of the upstream project, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the

upstream author or by DeepSeek. See NOTICE for the attribution and the list of changed files.
>
> *
*Two disclosures before you install.** (1) The plugin serves an **unauthenticated** loopback HTTP ro
ute: any local process can call it and spend your model quota. (2) The draft you polish — and, with
`contextAware` on, up to `contextMaxMessages` recent turns — is sent to your configured model provid
er. Both are detailed under Security & privacy.
English | 简体中文
## What it is
A plugin for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI. It adds a **polish** affordance to the composer: your dra
ft goes through a low-temperature rewrite pass served by the harness' own LLM service, the result ap
pears in a preview panel next to the original, and you choose to apply it, copy it, or throw it away
. Applying raises an undo bar that restores exactly what you had typed.
One npm package, two halves, following the dsh plugin conventions: a **host half** (Node) that owns
the HTTP route, the `/enhance` slash command and the settings namespace, and a **browser half** that
contributes the composer button, the preview panel, the undo bar and the configuration page.
## Why this fork exists
Upstream `0.2.x` of the harness changed three things that this plugin depended on, and the result wa
s a plugin that installed cleanly and then did nothing you could configure:
1. **Configuration silently disappeared.** dsh `0.2.x` derives a plugin's settings namespace from th
e `Config` schema the package exports and keeps only fields whose meta is `volatile`. Upstream marke
d none, so its entry was skipped entirely — no config page, no form, no way to write a value — while
the `installSection` / `installSettingsSection` wiring it used instead had already been removed fro
m the harness, so its compatibility probe returned without doing anything or logging anything. This

fork marks every field volatile and serves the namespace the way `0.2.x` expects.
[该节后续省略]
## Security & privacy
**1. The loopback HTTP route is unauthenticated by design.** Any process on your machine can `POST /
prompt-enhance/enhance` and spend your model quota. Per-caller authentication is not attempted. What
guards the route instead:
- **Socket fence** — requests from non-loopback peer addresses are refused (`127.0.0.1` / `::1` only

).
- **Host allowlist** — the `Host` header must be `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`, which defea
ts DNS rebinding (a rebound attacker domain keeps the loopback socket address but carries the attack

er's hostname and is refused). Responses are `cache-control: no-store`.
- **Origin gate** — browser

calls from non-local pages are refused.
- **Proxy rejection** — requests carrying `X-Forwarded-For`
or `Forwarded` are refused outright: those headers only exist when a proxy is in the path, which the

trust model does not cover.
- **Abuse caps** — a body cap derived from `maxInputChars` (with a `Con
tent-Length` fast reject), a sliding-window rate limit (`rateLimitPerMinute`, default 10, counting s
uccessful calls only) and a concurrency cap (`maxConcurrent`, default 2), both answering `429`. Both
counters live **in a single host process's memory**: several processes, a cluster or several profil
es mounting the plugin each count independently, so this plugin supports single-process deployments

and ships no shared rate-limit store.
- **Request-level timeouts belong to the host and Node** — the
plugin bounds the body size and the per-call `timeoutMs`; connection-level timeouts (headers / requ
est / keep-alive) are settings of the shared `http.Server` that a prefix route must not touch, so th

ey fall to the host and Node's defaults.
- **Not for reverse-proxy exposure** — if you put dsh web b
ehind a proxy that listens on the LAN, external callers look like loopback to the route and the fenc

e is moot. Do not expose a proxied host without adding your own authentication at the proxy.

## Compatibility
- **Harness:** `dsh.engines.dsh` = `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`. This fork drops pre-0.2 support: the setti
ngs wiring it replaced no longer exists in those lines. `dsh.engines` is advisory metadata read by t

he loader and plugin manager — it states support, it does not enforce it.
- **Node:** `^22.19.0 || >

=24.0.0` (for building from source).
- **Peers:** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm >=0.2.0-rc.2` as an **option
al** peer — it is a runtime module supplied by the dsh host and is not installed from npm (both `lib
/` bundles keep every package import external), so a host that does not provide it produces no insta
ll warning and the plugin reports a normal error at polish time instead of failing to load. `react`

/ `react-dom` `^18.2.0` are required and supplied by the web shell's module registry.
- **Other plug
ins on a `0.2.x` runtime:** the runtime's compatibility gate skips bundles whose peer ranges pin an
older `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` line (observed upstream with `dshmarket`, `dsh-find-plugin` and `dsh-bett
er-sidebar`). This package passes that gate.
